observation_summary: The EigenDecompositionImpl class produced incorrect eigenvalues due to an incorrect index calculation during an array flip operation.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the calculation of the index 'j' from '4 * n - 1' to '4 * (n - 1)'. This is a correction to the loop boundary logic within the algorithm responsible for flipping the work array. Since this is a procedural error in the implementation of the array manipulation algorithm, it is classified as Algorithm/Method.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows a change in the calculation of the variable 'j' used as the upper bound for the loop that flips the array.
The change from '4 * n - 1' to '4 * (n - 1)' corrects the loop iteration strategy for the array manipulation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing an assigned value, the root cause is the incorrect logic of the loop boundary calculation, which is a procedural/algorithmic concern.
There is no missing or incorrect guard or conditional check; the issue is the calculation of the loop limit itself.
